about: How far each renderer may sit from reSIDfp in tools/sid-engines/run_matrix.py --check. Renders are deterministic, so a measured value only moves when an engine or this app's use of it changes; the margins are there to let a harmless change through and stop a real one. Each override names the tune by file stem and says why it differs.

overrides.reason: libSidplayEZ plays $D418 volume-register samples on a 6581 about 2 dB louder than reSIDfp.
On an 8580 libSidplayEZ plays $D418 volume-register samples about 9 dB quieter than reSIDfp; the real 8580 barely reproduces them, and which emulation is closer is not settled.
The ladder ramps $D418 to silence at the end of every note, so the same 8580 volume-register difference as digi-8580 shapes its spectrum.
HVSC: reSIDfp's envelope differs on the fast arpeggios; chroma and band balance match closely.
HVSC: as Commando; subsong 10 also starts 50 ms earlier, the start-up difference described in the architecture document.
HVSC: an 8-bit digi, played about 1.7 dB quieter, the same register difference as digi-6581 in the other direction.

HVSC: three chips. The wrapper plays them as a centred mono mix (see the architecture document), where reSIDfp's two sides correlate at 0.88 for this tune. The chips are correlated, so the mix also plays about 1.2 dB louder.
Filter sweeps at full resonance on a 6581: libSidplayEZ's tuned 6581 filter (gain, curve, leakage) swells differently from reSIDfp's; 0.88 over 20 s, 0.84 over 30 s.
SIDLite plays 8580 volume-register samples about 4.5 dB louder than reSIDfp.
HVSC: SIDLite is a cheaper approximation; its envelopes diverge most on fast arpeggios.
HVSC: an 8-bit digi, played about 4 dB louder.
HVSC: multispeed, played about 3 dB louder.
HVSC: an NTSC RSID whose chroma similarity sits at 0.91.
HVSC: a BASIC tune; SIDLite starts it about 30 ms later.
SIDLite's 6581 filter is a simpler approximation; 0.69 over 20 s, 0.59 over 30 s.
